title: Does not getting enough sleep cause weight gain? What's the link
intro: Yes, less sleep can make you hungrier and make it harder to control your eating. The good news is, improving your sleep little by little can make your weight loss efforts easier.

sections.h: What happens when you lack sleep
sections.p: When you sleep less, the hormone that makes us hungry tends to go up and the fullness hormone tends to go down. You crave sweet and oily foods more. Your body is also tired, so you move less throughout the day.
Most adults need an estimated 7 to 9 hours of sleep. If you sleep 5 hours now, no need to jump straight to 8 hours. Add 15 to 30 minutes first and let it become a habit.
Limit coffee or tea after 3 pm. Put your phone a bit further from your bed 30 minutes before sleeping. Try to sleep and wake up at about the same time every day, including weekends.

sections.h: Days when you really lack sleep
sections.p: Some days can't be avoided, for example deadlines or a sick child. On these days, plan your meals earlier. Choose foods with protein and vegetables, and avoid walking into convenience stores aimlessly when tired.

If you get enough sleep but still feel very tired, or your weight goes up even though your eating and activity haven't changed, please see a doctor. Conditions like thyroid problems or PCOS can affect energy and weight, and need to be checked properly.

action: Set a 'bedtime' alarm 30 minutes before you want to sleep.
Swap afternoon coffee after 3 pm for plain water or caffeine-free tea.
Charge your phone outside the bedroom or away from your bed for 3 nights this week.
On days with less sleep, bring a packed lunch or plan your lunch menu in the morning.
myth: Many believe sleeping late at night itself causes weight gain. In fact, what matters more is getting too little sleep, along with the extra eating and less movement that usually come with it.

faq.q: Does a short afternoon nap help?
faq.a: A 15 to 20 minute nap can help your energy. Avoid napping too long or too late in the afternoon as it can disturb your night sleep.

faq.q: I work shifts, what should I do?
faq.a: Focus on total sleep and a dark, quiet room. Plan your meal times according to your shift, not other people's clock.

faq.q: My weight went up even though I eat the same. Why?
faq.a: Many factors can be involved, including sleep, stress, your menstrual cycle and health conditions like thyroid problems or PCOS. If it continues, please check with a doctor.
